channel.title: Crypto Record
channel.description: Crypto Record reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto market.

item.title: How Checksum Case Changes an Ethereum Address Search
item.description: Checksum casing adds one brief validation step to an Ethereum address search; the database lookup, network request and index account for almost all of the wait.

item.title: Why a Bridge Status Can Outlast a Wallet Transaction
item.description: A wallet receipt confirms one chain’s transaction; a bridge status follows the separate proof, checkpoint and release steps needed before funds arrive on the destination chain.

item.title: A Base DEX Pool’s Volume Is Visible; Its Organic Share Isn’t
item.description: A Base pool’s swap total is observable, but its organic share is not; routes, arbitrage and wallet loops mean volume needs context from depth and flow.

item.title: Renting Energy or Paying TRX for a TRON USDT Transfer
item.description: A TRON USDT transfer runs a smart contract, consumes Energy and Bandwidth, then uses staked resources, delegated Energy or a TRX burn to cover the bill.

item.title: SEC proposes conditional crypto self-custody for advisers and funds
item.description: The SEC proposed rules letting advisers and regulated funds self-custody some crypto assets under key-control, reporting and board-oversight safeguards.

item.title: Polygon PoS withdrawals take two transactions
item.description: A Polygon PoS withdrawal burns the token first, then releases the Ethereum asset after a validator checkpoint; plan for two transactions and a wait.

item.title: Set Aside Gas Before You Withdraw a Token
item.description: A token withdrawal needs the network’s fee currency as well as the token itself; check which chain runs the transaction and reserve enough before you send.

item.title: Five Steps to Fund a Manta Pacific Market-Maker Pool
item.description: Funding a Manta Pacific market-maker pool moves a token pair into a managed vault, where inventory and active liquidity support trading across selected price ranges.

item.title: How to Choose a Fast Route Back to Ethereum
item.description: The fastest route back to Ethereum depends on whether you need protocol settlement or a quicker liquidity exit, and what fees and trust assumptions you accept.

item.title: What Tor Hides When You Swap XMR
item.description: Tor can hide your IP address from a swap service, but it cannot hide swap timing, public-chain details, or order information a hosted operator receives directly.

item.title: Why Your Mantle Bridge Transfer Is Stuck
item.description: A Mantle transfer can wait at wallet approval, source-chain confirmation, message processing or the final withdrawal claim; its status tells you what to do next.

item.title: How to Compare Cross-Chain Swap Costs
item.description: A cross-chain swap’s real cost is the gap between its quoted and executed rate plus every network and route fee; compare the same output, not just the fee line.

item.title: Why a Polygon PoS Withdrawal Waits for a Checkpoint
item.description: A Polygon PoS withdrawal waits for a validator checkpoint, then an Ethereum claim; estimate the delay by tracking both stages and keeping gas ready.

item.title: SEC proposes crypto custody path for advisers and funds
item.description: The SEC proposed crypto custody rules for advisers and funds, with conditional self-custody and state trust companies as custodians under new safeguards.

item.title: What an XMR bridge changes when a wallet swap crosses chains
item.description: An xmr bridge routes value from a Monero wallet to an asset on another chain; the route and destination address determine what arrives in practice.

item.title: Tron Energy: Three Ways to Pay for Contract Calls
item.description: TRON contract calls use Energy for execution and Bandwidth for transaction data; you can stake for Energy, receive a delegation or let the network burn TRX.

item.title: What an Upgrade Costs: Smart Contract Energy for Beginners
item.description: An upgrade may deploy new code, switch a proxy pointer, or move contract state; each path uses network resources differently, and TRON meters execution as Energy.

item.title: Staking or Renting TRON Energy: Compare Cost and Control
item.description: Staking ties up TRX to build reusable Energy capacity; renting delegates a provider’s Energy for a short window, so usage frequency and timing decide which costs less.

item.title: Unstake TRX Without Losing Track of Energy
item.description: Unstaking TRX starts a waiting period and reduces your Energy stake; track each request, its expected release date and final withdrawal to avoid a resource gap.

item.title: How Monero Deposit Confirmations Work in Swap Integrations
item.description: A swap service detects an XMR deposit through its wallet scan, matches it to an order, then waits for block confirmations before releasing the other asset.
